# Temple & Webster and GrowthBook | Commercials, Proof of Concept, Platform Demo
Date: 2026-11-06 | Duration: 53.45000076293945m

## Summary
The discussion found that existing Optimizely logic can be migrated, including feature flags, rollouts, experiment splitting by user ID, visual web editing, and sticky bucketing using anonymous or device IDs with joined identity data. An approval workflow with RBAC publishing controls and human review was recommended. BigQuery can retain exposure events, join them with BI and revenue metrics, support variation-level conversion reporting, and enable direct SQL validation, A/A comparisons, and custom analysis. Stable customer tiers and developer-controlled targeting were preferred because changing attributes can reassign users unexpectedly. Commercially, licensing includes security, onboarding, training, and migration support; user-based pricing scenarios were discussed, with no experience-volume surcharge. Self-hosting lowers pricing but requires Temple Webster to manage DevOps, while BigQuery remains customer-controlled. The POC is planned to start November 16 for three weeks, with the decision target moved to December 16 and a follow-up scheduled for Tuesday.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Optimizely migration, Sticky bucketing, BigQuery experimentation, Self-hosted deployment, Proof of concept
